prompt:
Scene:
A top-down square photograph of an anti-fashion zine page on cream photocopier paper, moody desk lamp from the left. Light falls unevenly and the photocopy drum streaks are softer.

Subject:
An anti-fashion layout page: three cut-out editorial fashion photographs re-composed with deliberately wrong crops — one shows only legs with a torn top, another only a shoulder, another a cropped torso. Taped over each figure is a ballpoint drawn alternate outfit in sketchy lines. A grid of tiny cut-out patches of fabric magazine pages is pasted along the right margin. Scissor-scribbled scribbles connect them.

Important details:
Every cut is deliberately crude, cropping faces off at weird angles. Ballpoint over-drawings must feel confident but unpolished, with some hesitant double-lines. Fabric-texture patch collage must show actual photo-print grain from different source pages. Tape ends must curl up.

Use case:
Independent single image in the Collage Moods package, representing the anti-fashion deconstructionist voice.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no brand names, no recognizable model faces, no clean fashion photography, no vector drawings, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
